name: Shipping Box Assembly & Seal
description: Assemble a flat cardboard box, seal it with proper H-tape pattern, and prepare it for shipping — the standard process used in warehouses and fulfillment centers worldwide.

steps.instruction: Open the flat box and pop it into a rectangular shape. Hold it upright so you can see inside — it should form an open-top, open-bottom tube.
steps.visual_cue: Box is standing upright in a rectangular tube shape with both ends open.
common_errors: Box is still flat or only partially opened
Creases not fully bent to 90 degrees

steps.instruction: Fold the two SHORT flaps inward first. The short flaps are on the narrower sides of the box — they are noticeably smaller, roughly half the width of the long flaps. They MUST go in before the long flaps. Leave the two LONG flaps open for now.
steps.visual_cue: The user is showing the box opening. Two SMALLER flaps are folded inward (flat against the inside). Two LARGER flaps are still sticking out or standing up — NOT folded yet. The opening is NOT fully closed because the long flaps are still up. If the opening looks fully closed or you see two large flaps folded down, the wrong flaps were folded first.
during_action_cues: WATCH which flaps the user reaches for FIRST. Short flaps are on the NARROW ends of the box — they are visibly smaller. Long flaps are on the WIDE sides — they are larger and span the full width.
If you see the user grabbing or folding a flap that spans the FULL WIDTH of the box (the longer dimension), STOP THEM IMMEDIATELY — that is a long flap, not a short flap. The long flaps must go LAST.

CRITICAL VISUAL CHECK: After flaps are folded, look at the box from above. If two large flaps are folded down and you can see the interior between them, those are LONG flaps folded incorrectly. Correct state: two SMALL flaps folded with LARGE flaps still sticking up.
If the folded flaps cover most of the box opening, those are long flaps (WRONG). If the folded flaps are small and leave a large gap in the center, those are short flaps (CORRECT).
common_errors: Folding long flaps first instead of short flaps — this is the #1 mistake. Look at the SIZE of the folded flaps: if they span the full width of the box, they are long flaps and were folded in the wrong order. The bottom will be structurally weak.
Flaps not folded fully flat against the bottom

VISUAL INDICATOR OF WRONG ORDER: If you see two large flaps folded down with the box interior visible between them (like looking into a slot), the long flaps were folded first. Correct: two small flaps folded with two large flaps still upright.

steps.instruction: Now fold the two LONG flaps down over the short flaps. They should meet in the center, forming a flat sealed bottom with a seam running down the middle.
steps.visual_cue: Bottom is fully closed. Long flaps meet at center seam. Surface is flat. No gaps visible between the two long flaps.
common_errors: Long flaps overlapping unevenly — one side sticking out more than the other
Gap between the two long flaps at the center seam
Flaps not pressed flat — bottom still has a bump or ridge

steps.instruction: Apply tape along the center seam where the two long flaps meet. Run the tape the full length of the seam, extending about 2-3 inches past each edge of the box.
steps.visual_cue: Single strip of tape running along the full center seam of the bottom, extending past both edges.
common_errors: Tape does not cover the full seam length
Tape not extended past the box edges

steps.instruction: Apply the H-tape: add two short strips of tape across each end of the box bottom, perpendicular to the center seam. This reinforces the edges where the flaps meet the sides. The center tape plus these two cross-strips form an H shape.
steps.visual_cue: H-tape pattern visible on box bottom: one long center strip plus two short perpendicular strips at each end, forming the letter H.
common_errors: Cross-strips not covering the flap-to-side seam
Only taping the center without the H reinforcement

steps.instruction: Flip the box right-side up so the sealed bottom is on the table. The box should stand on its own with the opening facing up, ready to be loaded. Give it a gentle press to confirm the bottom is solid.
steps.visual_cue: Box is standing upright on its sealed bottom, open top facing up, stable and ready for packing.
common_errors: Bottom pops open or feels weak when pressed
Box is lopsided or not standing straight
